author: haiku
label: climb-02-01
changes: Decision 12 and the diagram: Origin check runs first and returns 403 with no database access and nothing recorded. Added a 403 row to the response matrix (Q1).
Decision 13: only a successful login deletes the session the incoming cookie points to, in the same transaction. A failed login leaves the cookie and session alone (Q2).
Decision 3 and the diagram: the app hashes the cookie value on every protected request and on logout, and a malformed value is treated as no session with no query (Q3).
Decision 14 and the schema: sessions reference users with ON DELETE CASCADE. The protected request uses user_id from the UPDATE and does not reload the users row (Q4).
Decision 9 and the lockout states: a lock blocks the correct password too, for the full 15 minutes. A success can only clear a lock that has expired (Q5).
Decision 9, the diagram and the response matrix: the 429 includes a Retry-After header, and the cookie is untouched (Q6).
Lockout states: added a worked example showing that old failures outside the 10-minute window do not count toward the next lock (Q7).

Decision 4 and the schema: login lock checks and failure timestamps use clock_timestamp(), because now() is fixed at transaction start and the advisory lock may wait. Found while answering Q5 and Q7. The expiry checks still use now().
Decision 12: the Origin check compares against the configured public origin, not the Host header, because a load balancer may rewrite Host (Q8).

Merged the separate 'why unknown email and wrong password match' and lockout trade-off notes into shorter paragraphs. Replaced the repeated per-state explanations with one response matrix. Moved the TLS question into a single open-questions list at the end.
Removed the repeated explanations of cookie attributes and session limits that appeared in both decisions and state notes. Kept each rule in one place.
Decision 6: wrote out the login insert values (created_at, last_seen_at, absolute and idle expiry) and the protected-request UPDATE as SQL, so the expiry rule is in the file itself (Q12, Q13).
Decision 8: added the failure-count query, showing that it includes the new row and uses clock_timestamp() (Q15).
Decision 9: the locked path rolls back before the 429 is sent, because nothing was written there (Q10).
Decision 10: the advisory lock key is hashtext of the trimmed, lowercased email, and it is released at COMMIT or ROLLBACK, with every path ending the transaction before responding (Q9, Q10).
Sequence diagram: the locked branch now shows ROLLBACK before the 429, and the advisory lock step names the hashtext key (Q9, Q10).
State and rules: added a Login page rule that says GET /login always shows the form, with no session check, Origin check or cookie change (Q11).

Failure behaviour: the login storage-failure rule now lists the steps that can fail, says a lock row that cannot be read is a 503 and never treated as no lock, and says Set-Cookie is sent only after COMMIT succeeds (Q14).
Merged the session-states list into decision 6, which already stated the limits. Removed the separate "Session limits" and "Session states" sections that repeated it.
Merged decision 15 (status codes) with the response table. The table already lists each status, so the duplicate prose was cut and only the 303 and Cache-Control rules were kept.
Moved the GET /login rule (form always shown, no session read, no Origin check, cookie untouched) under the response table, so it sits with the other response rules instead of its own section.
Merged the "Why unknown email and wrong password match" section into one note under the response table. Corrected its wording: the 429 and 503 do not depend on whether the account exists.
Removed the "Lockout states" list (Clear, Counting, Locked) and kept the 00:00 to 00:24 example, which shows the same sliding-window behaviour in one place.
Merged the "Lockout trade-off" section into the open boundary on targeted lockout, since both described the same accepted risk.
Shortened the storage-failure bullet by listing the login steps once, and removed the repeated sentence about the failed lock read.
Combined "Open boundaries" and "Open questions" into one section at the end, as the skill asks, and labelled the TLS item as open.
Shortened the Redis rationale in decision 1 and the wording of decisions 4, 5, 9, 10 and 13. No values, rules or responses were changed.
Moved the schema sketch to the end, after the open questions, so the decisions and diagram come first. The Mermaid sequence diagram was left unchanged, since the brief requires it.
holes: Q8: What do the two app instances sit behind, and how do requests reach them? The document mentions a load balancer only in passing. Does TLS end there, and does that affect the Secure cookie and Origin check? (author: The brief does not say where TLS terminates, or whether the load balancer rewrites the Host header. The app sets Secure on the cookie either way, since the browser sees HTTPS. The Origin check needs the public scheme and host, so decision 12 now compares against a configured public origin, not the Host header. The exact load balancer setup is not known, and it is listed under open questions.)
